review: In short - Awesome, awesome, awesome remake to the awesome SH classing, and finally some breathe of life to the franchise.   ✅ Pros + Bloober Team respects original source material and enhances it greatly. + This has everything that made SH2 great and improving pretty much everything that can be improved without hurting the original magic: Better combat, better graphics, better voice acting, awesome soundtrack + Great scared, eerie tone and psychological fear + Can easily be a strong entry point for newbies to Silent Hill or survival horror games. + Difficulty feels fair and balanced while still challenging, on Normal (Action\Puzzles) + There's puzzles difficultly and combat difficulty, yay!  ⚖️ If that's your thing: +/- Classic Survival Horror games can at many times feel like closed doors simulator, and the remake doesn't so anything to change this (Which I personally didn't expect or mind) +/- Combat is greatly improved but still feels clunky, in a genre-fitting way I believe +/- Linear and relatively short (As pretty much most SH games)  ❌ Cons None!   Longer version no one reads:  I'm finishing this game with a sigh of relief, as looks like at least for the time being, Silent Hill is back on track.  After having played and loved almost all main Silent Hill games (Besides Downpour, on which I didn't get my hands on yet) (And yeah, I loved even Homecoming!), Seemed Silent Hill went dead forever, and then we got.... Well, Silent Hill Ascension, which was.... Ugh, let's not get into it. But then we got THIS.  I was expecting the remake for a long time, and having also played and enjoyed The Medium by Bloober I also had faith they'd do a good job, but still had doubts as their previous games weren't so much action oriented.  I guess making a remake is somewhat easier in that case as they didn't have to create something completely anew but more of re-doing some already existing powerful source material. While I'm not that hardcore fan which completed every SH 20 times - I've only completed the original once, and that was many years ago, so I cannot point out all the differences etc. Still in my honest opinion, I feel Bloober did a perfect job in this one - much respect to the source material, they're really managed to capture the magic and horror of the original game, preserving what worked and improving everything that could be improved - The soundtrack remains loyal to the original with some musical overhaul from time to time (which I liked). The new voice overs work well and capture the eeriness and weirdness of the original characters. Graphics are obviously overhauled and look modern and pretty darn good (and scary!). Script and story remained mostly (if not completely) the same as far as I can remember, which is a good thing. Combat is greatly improved and feels mostly great, while still keeping that survival-horror awkwardness (which some may feel is a "bug" and some a "feature", but I think it serves the game just right). I think some puzzles were replaced but I've enjoyed the whole experienced on Normal from beginning to an end. Quality of scares does not fall short from original game and there's just the right balance between jump scares and some freaking psychological fear (Oh and that damn limbs monster got me squeaking every time!)  I feel this game can also serve as a great entry point for newcomers to both Silent Hill and\or Survival Horror, this is truly a modern version capturing all the best things about Silent Hill, in my opinion. I can see why some might prefer a more Resident-Evil-ish direction when SH games can sometimes feel like closed doors simulator, but hey, isn't that part of Survival Horroring?  Already expecting to play Silent Hill F although not by same dev, but seems it's doing pretty well by the reviews, and mainly I'm very happy having some attention and actual resources going towards this series, and very hopeful we'll keep seeing some more quality stuff from the franchise (And I wouldn't mind another remake as well (=;  )

review: Easily one of the best horror games I've played in a while. The pace, the game loop, graphics, sound, story and environments. It's the right amount of scary without being stressful. Not too forgiving with resources, yet generous enough. Puzzles are fun. Fighting mechanics are intuitive.  I've been a fan of horror games since the first Resident Evil came out. But for some reason I just could not get into Silent Hill, despite being such a popular franchise. And it was not because I didn't want it, but because circumstances never let it happen.  It was until the PS3 era when I first got to play one: Silent Hill Homecoming. While that game is universally hated, it was my first Silent Hill and I found it to be an amazing horror game. The only negatives I could find was the bad controls and overall performance, which was not very good.  I don't feel that this game is that different in terms of content, but just the fact that it is very well polished and the graphics have been improved, make it a much more enjoyable experience.  I don't have much to say in terms of lore and such because this is my second Silent Hill, and my first mainline title. Compared to the only Silent Hill I've played before, it feels like it follows the same formula (I know I'll get destroyed by SH fans for saying this).  I never expected to enjoy it as much as I have. I don't think I can find any negatives about this game. Even performance has been solid. No crashes, stuttering, FPS dips, etc. Maxed out graphics, 1440p, RT on, 120fps. And it plays great with a generic Xbox One controller.

review: Genuinely the best survival horror game in since probably re7 imo. The game is gorgeous with RT on and the sound design might be the best in a horror game i've played. Be warned, its not a "fun" story nor is it really a fun game to play.   Its not a jump scare heavy type of game in the vein of visage or similar but instead it simply uses dread & suspense that doesnt go away, from the apartment section to the hospital(and beyond) it simply never really gives you a time to breath.  The combat is mostly ok with a similar feeling to RE2 remake but just alot slower in general, James isnt really the quickest character to move around or hit things with. There's not alot of enemy variation either but i think its more ok than usual since combat isnt constant(maybe except for the prison area) and while i enjoyed the combat it does drag on a bit towards the end. Healing items & ammunition might be given a bit to often tbh, i think i had around 30 heals throughout the last areas to the end of the game which made some areas & bosses very trivial and easy to fight through.  I think James is my favourite game protagonist in a long time, he is not perfect in the slightest but you cant help but you cant help but to feel sorry for the dude, he is just depressed as hell and is not having a good time throughout the game.   The only real downside is the length, i finished the game in about 14.5 hours which could have and should have been cut down a few hours(specially parts of the hospital & the labyrinth). Those areas that drag on are not bad at all but just feels a bit boring to go  through after a while(thinking of the otherworld hospital here etc).  Its a 9/10 for me and a actual must play for most people, even tho its a scary game i think the story and its themes are things people very much should experience and also talk about.

review: We need more horror games tackling themes of mental health. Silent Hill 2 isn't just an unsettling game, it's an emotional one. It's not afraid of diving into the darkest parts of the human psyche, and I felt some of these themes were something that I (and most likely others) have experienced ourselves.  The atmosphere is oppressive and suffocating, the ambience and immersion is some of the best I've experienced in a video game. This is a slow-paced game where you soak everything in and explore as much you can, with the game rewarding you for it. There are multiple endings that are entirely determined by [i]how[/i] you play. I won't get much into it, but [i]everything[/i] you do will decide which ending path you're headed towards, so keep that in mind.  The combat is satisfying and does its job. My most used weapon was a steel pipe (I prefer melee combat) and whacking down the monsters never got old. The enemies were grotesque, with the boss designs taking everything to a horrifyingly new level. I guess my only criticism is that I felt the game was a bit [i]too[/i] generous with the ammo and health supply (I like to struggle and suffer), but it doesn't take away from the game at all.  The music is just amazing. We all know how good Akira Yamaoka is at this point, I'll just leave it at that.  The voice acting is phenomenal. Luke Roberts not getting the recognition he deserved for his portrayal of James is a genuine crime. You could hear the uncertainty, hurt, confusion, frustration, trauma, in every line - it just felt [i]real[/i], with one of the endings being an all-time performance in a video game.  Anyways, I think I've gone on for long enough. I absolutely love this game - so much so that I'm planning to go for all endings and try to achieve 100%. I have Silent Hill f ready to play once I'm done and I can't wait. I'm glad Silent Hill has had a resurgence and I'm hoping they can maintain this level of quality for future games (I can't wait for the Silent Hill 1 remake).  Play this game.

review: Never ever have i played a better game in the horror genre than Silent Hill 2 (Remake). The psychological displeasure of this game is underlined with an atmosphere like no other. There are very few jumpscares, but the ones that actually are in the game are phenomenal. Because of this circumstance you always have to stay sharp and concentrated. But the true fact that makes this game so interesting is its unmatched ambient. Fog, noises, the people you meet, the town itself. You always ask yourself - "whats even happening here?" until the plot gets revealed and you do your own research afterwards, which is absolutely mindblowing once you realize the true nature of all the protagonists.  The little details are unmatched for this genre. Facial expressions, dialogue hints, metaphors - you name it. After finishing the game I was still very invested and to this day still I occasionally read lore or watch videos about the true meaning of many scenes, enemies, the main characters etc. even tho I finished the game nearly a year ago.  Combat is intense and very fair. It can feel slow at certain times, but thats exactly why fighting is so pleasurable. The enemies are terrifying, boss battles are insanely well done with great variety of attack-patterns. Puzzles are extremely smart designed. Pacing is phenomenal. The story is one of the best written stories not only in the gaming-world, but in fiction/theater/movies in general and i truly mean it.  I will 100% replay this and get a physical copy for my PS5 too.  This is in my Top 5 Games of all time, if not even higher.  Must play.  10/10

review: Hauntingly beautiful.  Silent Hill 2 is gorgeous in the most terrifying way possible. I mean, it is scary: the whole journey, guaranteed to be over 12 hours long on a first run, is a long, slow descent into the depths of a post-industrial hell made of rusted metal, bloodied cloth, deformed enemies, and non-euclidean geography. A sizeable portion of my enjoyment of this game lay in its aesthetics, and holy hell, did it deliver. Floors lead to empty voids, interior ceilings may or may not exist, Silent Hill itself turns inside-out and adopts the appearance of machinery's interiors, and claustrophobia reigns supreme. Whether in the [spoiler]normal town[/spoiler] and its desolate, sinister, isolating aura, or the [spoiler]Otherworld[/spoiler] and its oppressive, screeching, decaying premise, the modern visuals never failed to disappoint.  At the same time, Silent Hill 2 is a captivating sight to behold: the story is utterly captivating and compelling, and seeing James Sunderland's slog through his rotting iron purgatory, replete with guilt, punishment, and cruel metaphors, will be hard for me to forget. From Half-Life 2 to Resident Evil 4 to Spec Ops: The Line, I've always loved the long, nearly-unbroken journey across a vast space, learning more about the characters as they overcome greater trials, and SH2 is no exception. Never played the original, so I can't say how accurate or faithful it is, but it doesn't really matter that much to me. The underlying themes of [spoiler]guilt, trauma, and active repression of memories over an atrocious but darkly-understandable action in the face of watching a loved one slowly die with no hope for a cure[/spoiler] is a series off raw gut-punches, wrought with disturbing visual metaphors in the environmental, enemy, and atmospheric design.  The realistic aspects of Silent Hill 2 were well-received; the voice acting and dialogue stayed perfectly believable, and the acting itself was excellent throughout. Every character was memorable: James and Pyramid Head for obvious reasons, but Maria's, Eddie's, and Laura's performances gave the game a perfectly surreal and unsettling atmosphere. Combat isn't particularly hard if you're good at resource management, but on the hardest difficulty, it's not easy either. Preserving bullets and medical supplies is crucial, but if you're diligent with melee, saving up a few dozen bullets or so is entirely doable. They'll be needed during boss fights. Puzzles aren't hard either, but if they're not your thing, the experience of walking back and forth between rooms to find trinkets for hours won't be overly fun. This game is a masterpiece to me, though, and a gold-standard remake of a classic psychological horror game that's guaranteed to stick around in a player's brain for years.

review: Playing Silent Hill 2 Remake on PC felt like stepping into a nightmare I didn’t want to wake from. The graphics are absolutely stunning—every foggy street and decaying hallway looks disturbingly real. I kept stopping just to take it all in, even when I knew something awful was lurking nearby.  Combat surprised me. It’s intense and nerve-wracking in the best way. Every encounter feels like a fight for survival, especially when ammo runs low and you’re forced to rely on whatever’s in reach. The sound design makes it even worse—in a good way. The ambient noise, the music, the way monsters groan and shuffle—it all got under my skin.  But what really stuck with me was the story. James’s journey is still one of the most haunting and emotionally raw narratives I’ve ever played. It doesn’t just scare you—it makes you think. I found myself reflecting on guilt, grief, and denial long after I shut the game off. That said, I’m really hoping they release the Born From A Wish DLC soon. Maria’s story adds so much depth, and without it, her character feels incomplete. I want to see her side of things—her pain, her motives.  All in all, this remake was incredible. It’s beautiful, terrifying, and deeply human.

review: Having played through the game............. what can I say.  I played silent hill 2 when it came out. It was a masterpiece of it's time. In the end..... good game...... just not a very good...... specifically silent hill game.  The magic of team silent was lost at 4, and it's never been quite the same since.

review: I've long wanted to play the remake of one of my favorite games. However, it so happened that I only just finished the entire playthrough - and coincidentally, I'm writing this review on its first anniversary.  Firstly, I still can't believe this game was actually released. I bought it as a way of thanking Team Silent for giving the world such a unique series of games (which, among other things, influenced me). Secondly, I realized I’d be getting a remake of the second installment as well.  It's important to note that, simply due to the unavailability of both retro consoles and original game discs, it would have been difficult for the average player to experience the originals. Now, a new generation of players unfamiliar with the series can explore a modernized version in a convenient format.  I didn't have the chance to try the original game with its authentic gameplay experience. For enthusiasts like me, the Enhanced Edition was created, immersing me in the world of Silent Hill - and with that experience in mind, I constantly compared it to the remake. And you know what? Bloober Team managed to capture almost the entirety of that same atmosphere. During my first playthrough, I couldn’t believe I was reliving the same familiar story. You experience the same emotions as before - from the ambient soundscape of the quiet town (thanks again to the incomparable Akira Yamaoka for the soundtrack) to the oppressive atmosphere of the otherworldly realm.  And indeed, knowing every plot twist didn’t make the game boring at all. On the contrary, the developers almost completely redesigned the levels, making the familiar story feel fresh again. This makes it more engaging even for seasoned players who know the original by heart. The story itself hasn’t undergone any major changes - which is good for both newcomers who want to explore this project and returning fans who simply want to immerse themselves in the same world once more.  One downside is that the game runs on Unreal Engine 5. While I’ll admit the graphics look incredible, the visuals were so demanding that the gameplay suffered from constant frame-rate drops and general instability (which was actually one of the reasons why it took me so long to complete the game). For those with slower PCs, I recommend launching the game with the parameter “-dx11.” Naturally, this disables many of the engine’s advanced features, but it ensures a much more stable experience - at least, that’s what worked for me. The choice of engine is a topic for debate, but this review isn’t about that. The most important thing is that I was able to fully enjoy the game.  In conclusion, the Silent Hill 2 Remake is exactly what it should be. It preserves the spirit and atmosphere of the original while adapting the gameplay to a modern over-the-shoulder format. This gives players a new sense of freedom when controlling James, along with redesigned level architecture and new puzzles. If the reader is faced with the choice of playing the remake instead of the original, I can only encourage that decision - because the developers have meticulously preserved the soul of the game while adapting it to modern standards.  Thank you for reading. Peace to all.

review: this game is REALLY good, but... THE PERFORMANCE. I cannot stress enough how terribly this game runs. I have a good computer- maybe not quite "good" by today's standards, but it can run similar games like Resident Evil 4, 7 and 2, the Dead Space remake, and Amnesia: The Bunker just fine. What the genuine hell is the excuse for this game suddenly dropping to like, fifteen frames a second? Would it have killed them to add some loading screens? Would it have hurt to provide any good options for lowering the visual quality for the sake of performance- because that's what really irks me. I'm fine with my game not really looking the best it could. I'd love for it to look the best it can, but we don't always get what we want, do we? It becomes a genuine problem for me, though, when in the middle of fighting an enemy or even BOSS, my frames tank and i can barely even play the game. I don't even know what causes some of the frame drops. Loading new areas, of course, but randomly the framerate just kicks the bucket and I don't know why. It's something that I dealt with- I never had too many issues BECAUSE of the framerate but GOD it was annoying and genuinely hurt the experience for me. This is unacceptable- a SEVENTY DOLLAR SURVIVAL HORROR GAME that can't even reach 60 FPS unless you're staring directly at a corner. How did the game ship like this? Better yet- how has the game gone an entire YEAR without them adding adequate graphics and optimization settings, or fixing the source of the issue? Again, this is unacceptable. Visually this game isn't even like, stunning or anything. It's just realistic and it has good art direction, which doesn't necessitate a billion polygons and rays of light or whatever the hell even causes the abysmal framerate anyway.  Outside of the performance, Silent Hill 2 is a PHENOMENAL game. review: I am an avid Silent Hill fan, I have played every Silent Hill game up until now.  This remake of the beloved PS2 Silent Hill 2 game is a perfect update to a beloved story in the franchise. The cinematics, character interactions, audio, graphics, and environment truly immerse the player in this horror masterpiece.  The only thing I didn't enjoy as much were the battles with enemies, especially without guns. Melee weapons are cumbersome to use and strafing type battling is very disorienting. Aside from this, everything else was perfect.  Puzzles were challenging, and the highlight of the game definitely was the exploration. Often you would come into a new level and check all the doors available to you, while clearing out enemies. The game did a good job alerting you to the locations of key items and puzzles or treasure chests.  The game is pretty dark overall, which adds to the sense of dread as vision in some underground or indoor settings is severely curtailed. The radio works to enhance the sense of anxiousness as it alerts you to incoming enemies as you explore.  The best part of the game definitely is towards the end, where the nightmare sections are vibrant, varied, and perfectly designed to fill you with nightmares. The boss battles also are difficult and epic.  The developers have done great justice to this game. I am very happy with the results.  It is highly recommended for all fans of horror games. Still do give the original PS2 game a play, it is a very different kind of game than this one.

review: Silent Hill 2 is one of the greatest games ever made, let alone one of the greatest Survival Horror games. It doesn't matter whether we are talking about the original or this remake. That still holds true.  The story of James Sunderland looking for his dead wife who he receives a letter from is just an incredible set up. The strange surreal nature of the character interactions, the incredible atmosphere provided by the town of Silent Hill, and the way the story unfolds were a deeply affecting experience that I will never forget. I am happy to report that this remake delivers even HARDER on the original vision of the game. It feels like exactly the game that they would have made with better technology and budget. The performances of every character are flawless without completely removing the awkward nature of the original.  You don't need me to tell you that the game is absolutely gorgeous. The town looks so real. It really feels like a place you could go to. The graphics look crisp and detailed up close and properly obscured by fog in the distance. All of the grotesque details of every environment are expertly crafted in the otherworld segments. Many moments of high resolution disgust to experience. The redesigns of the characters have been criticized by some, particularly Angela. They must have made some changes before release based on feedback because now she looks pretty much exactly the way she should. Meanwhile, Maria's redesign I think is perfect and does a much better job of portraying her character. The original soundtrack also makes a reappearance with some minor updates which are completely welcome. By the way, why the HELL does it not have a photo mode??  Another thing that has been updated from the original is the combat. I am sorry to tell you, all of the praise you have heard about the original game's combat is completely unwarranted. I say this as someone who loves that game, but being able to completely stun lock enemies as long as you keep attacking even on the harder difficulties is not really "gameplay." Now in this game you actually have to conserve ammo and use your melee weapon and switch between that and your guns on the fly. Dodging is also a thing and works well. Perfect for a survival horror game. Though the puzzles were great in the original, this game's puzzles are even better. They're hard to figure out and you feel pretty smart once you do.  All of this comes together as an incredible package. I understand to those who feel really deep nostalgia for the original game might be upset by some minor changes or feel that this game lacks some soul. I'm sorry, but I can't agree at all. This game is beautiful and respectful to the original and it has been improved in nearly every single way. Please play it!

review: Short version, Silent Hill 2's remake is one of the best games I've ever played and is a perfect entry spot for those uncomfortable with learning the old games' tank controls. It will make you feel dirty, sad and contemplative, as it should.  the long version...  Speaking as newly minted Silent Hill fan, going through the entire series (largely in release order), I can't speak fully either as a SH veteran with a long history nor as someone completely fresh to the franchise, being caught somewhere in the middle. That said, the original SH2 was frankly a disappointment the first time I played through it. Heralded as one of the greatest horror games and stories in video games, I knew I was alone in this. It wasn't its gameplay, atmosphere or pacing, mind you. The game's excellent and arguably the best of the first three judging by those elements alone. And that's coming from someone that adored first game and really liked 3 but 2... 2's story took awhile to warm on me as I just found OG James's insufferable.  Now, let's be clear. I'm really not one of those folks who hates sad and or weak main characters. My issue instead was that I found OG James creepy for most of my playthrough and I just couldn't sympathies with him. He felt like the archetypal (and I hate using this term) "nice guy", someone who's only nice because he feels like that's what's expected of him or to his benefit, but actually felt nothing towards others. Remake James meanwhile I wouldn't mind hanging out with. He'd be quiet and there would be "something" off about him, but I would just put it off as him going through a rough patch. Of course, things are complicated and there's more to both versions of James, but the differences being if I found out Remake James did something bad, I'd be shocked, while with OG James I'm just waiting to find out something. Many fans of the OG will argued that James is supposed to be off-putting as is the rest of the cast, but for me personally, it's a more effective atmosphere that I'm dreading the monsters and horrors, not encountering other people. There's still plenty off about the cast of SH2 Remake, but it's a lot more subtle, in large parts thanks to advanced motion capture and amazing performances, and I much prefer it. Gameplay wise, the remake is superb. I don't think anyone gonna deny that the remake is vast improvement in combat, which was pretty easy in the original outside of one or two annoying enemy types. Combat feels hefty and tense, making me calculate and weigh my options and resources when I spot enemies ahead or have to react in panic when I'm jumped. Boss battles are now actually boss fights, while the original killed whatever tension I might have had with everyone's favourite, pyramid head, in his long and annoying first boss fight where you just dodge his slow attacks for awhile in a small room.   Puzzles are mostly pretty good, with only the occasional headache that made me like I was going insane (I played on Hard puzzles for reference). The environments are absolutely top tier in industry, feeling large and allowing for those wonderful metroidvana brain clicks when areas loop back, but are simultaneously highly detailed and uncomfortably tight when fitting. The visuals teams deserves big credit for making Silent Hill's Otherworld tie a little more into other games versions of it whilst making it very distinctly its own between the wetness and overwhelming filth. Honest to god, part of me is disappointed James doesn't retain any grim and crap he gets covered in, but I'm also aware it would be have been tiring for him to look like 90% of the game without them adding a shower mechanic or something.  Some might be wondering how scary the game is, but I'm the wrong person to ask. I haven't found any third person games scary at this point in my life, with only SH3 getting to me in brief moments to its sound and creature designs hitting a personal nerve. That said, SH2 remake did make me jump the odd time (the mannequins can go to hell, thank you) and the grossness certainly made me uncomfortable, especially in those quick times event. Its sound design is also amazing and whomever made the choice to add those noises to the mannequins deserves a raise. So yeah, I won't call SH2 Remake scary, certainly uncomfortable and occasionally giving the odd surprise, but your mileage will vary if you're not desensitized to 90% of horror like I am.  Frankly, the only criticisms I can imagine someone having with this game are due to its interpretations of the story (which is highly subjective), its slower pace (fair, but the original had moments that were too fast, like meeting Angela then Eddie in the labyrinth), and if its combat is too powering or not enough (again, a highly subjective matter). That's rather incredible I feel for a game that could have gone so wrong and been rushed to make Konami a quick buck (*ahem* Downpour, Homecoming, etc), but Bloober Team absolutely delivered and for my money, made a great game even better.  I excited yet terrified for their upcoming Silent Hill 1 remake.

review: Silent Hill 2 is simply one of the greatest horror games ever made. What makes it so special to me is how much of the fear comes from inside, not outside. The monsters, the fog, the town itself — everything feels like a reflection of James’s mind, his guilt, his grief, his need for punishment. It’s not just about being scared, it’s about being unsettled all the way down, and that’s what makes it unforgettable.  I love how everything in the game means something. Pyramid Head isn’t just a monster, he’s James’s guilt given form. The environments aren’t just creepy, they feel like memories rotting away. Even the other characters you meet feel like echoes of trauma, each carrying their own despair. It’s all so layered, and the more you think about it, the darker it gets.  The story is devastating. James isn’t some action hero — he’s broken, and as the truth unravels you realize just how tragic it all is. It’s rare for a game to make you feel horror and heartbreak at the same time, but Silent Hill 2 does it better than anything else I’ve played. The atmosphere, the pacing, the sound design, Akira Yamaoka’s music — every piece comes together perfectly.  It’s clunky sometimes, sure, especially the combat, but honestly I don’t even care. The awkwardness just makes the game feel heavier, slower, more suffocating. It’s part of the experience.  Silent Hill 2 isn’t just a horror game. It’s a masterpiece about grief, guilt, memory, and how far people will go to hide from or face the truth. It’s stuck with me more than any other horror game ever has, and probably always will.  Thanks Team Silent! :)

review: An outstanding game. A faithful yet innovative remake of the original 2001 title.   This game is haunting, melancholic, and thought-provoking. The themes were nailed perfectly here; it is a clear project of passion and appreciation for the original material. Every bit screams that it was hand-crafted intentionally, every detail well thought out and designed with purpose, both during gameplay, cutscenes, and even in menus. This remake features a surprisingly impressive range of accessibility customisation. I cannot state enough how massively appreciated Bloober Team's careful thought to implement every one of these options is. More on this later.  This game offers a special experience within the survival-horror genre due to its especially rich storytelling. I admire Silent Hill 2 for its thoughtful attention to detail, symbolism, and the way the environments tell the story more often than things being spoken outright. I devoured this game for the way it let me sink into it and become a part of the world, carefully dissecting each piece of it and pondering its meaning. Some things were surely more obvious than others, but I loved its constant invitation to *dig*.   Silent Hill 2 is stunning and immersive in both exploration and cinematics. Across the board, the vocal performances, animations, etc were completely spot-on decisions. If some award is not won for this, I'll honestly be shocked.  The combat isn't a particularly stand-out feature, lacking specialty and depth, but those aspects of the game are not intended to be the focus, and frankly never have been. Atmosphere and narrative have always been the focus of Silent Hill, and what makes the series so memorable and iconic to this very day. The original game was formatted in a way that required the player to control James from an almost birds-eye angle, the camera being fixed in one corner of the room. This lead to somewhat wonky controls, and makes for iconic yet frustrating gunplay in retrospect. Somewhat drawing from this, the Silent Hill 2 remake features equally "vanilla" gunplay, without bells and whistles that overcomplicate things without reason. The guns are slightly inaccurate seemingly regardless of how you attempt to handle them, but perhaps this was entirely intentional. Is James an experienced gun wielder, or is he just desperately attempting to fend off these walking nightmares?  I spent a big portion of the beginning of my play-through chuckling away as I charged about Silent Hill, smashing car windows and breaking into stores, as well as repeatedly stomping enemies' bodies after they'd jumps-cared me. This game was immense fun from start to finish, all while being perfectly disturbing, tense, and heartbreaking when it should have been.  But this enjoyment was not without some frustration.  I played on Medium settings, with certain features set to "off" where possible; a routine setup for my system regardless of the game.   Originally the iconic fog that has settled over Silent Hill didn't exist solely to create atmosphere, rather was a clever strategy to assist the original system - the PlayStation One -  in rendering nearby surroundings, and eliminate the need to focus on anything too far away. It was a smart benefit to the system at the time, yet now it's ironically a resource hog. The mist itself is not a solid block as it used to be, now causing frames to drop because of particle effects. I couldn't help but find this slightly comedic, given the original design purpose.   Despite my PC being well within (actually above) the recommended specifications, I try to eliminate as much as possible to allow for some breathing room whilst still maintaining visual quality. Unfortunately, despite my attempts to optimise the game, I suffered consistent frame-drops and stuttering from start to finish.   I was forced to lower the difficulty of combat because on many occasions I either died or wasted ammunition due to the performance issues. It did remove a layer of intensity on numerous occasions, as the briefly frozen frames provided a crack through the immersion so I could recover or react to whatever may have been going on at times.  Accessibility is something that I am deeply passionate about. I advocate for as much accessibility in gaming as possible wherever I can. I have made numerous complaints across different games regarding the inability to customise features to suit one's preferences or to assist one's disability. Games should be fun to experience, first and foremost. I wholeheartedly believe that everyone deserves a fair shot at something they aim to achieve if it's realistically within reach and they have the drive to do so.  Silent Hill 2 remake well and truly blew me away as one of the most inclusive and carefully considered games I've played personally. I cannot quite articulate how thrilled I was. It was truly something special to browse the menu and feel cared for, something myself and many others experience all to little of within gaming. Bloober Team's systems allowed customisation of a wide range of settings.   These included (but were not at all limited to):  HUD - Reticle Visibility (Off/Minimal/Dynamic - displays a range of reticle shapes and designs for various weapons) - Reticle Thickness (Thin/Normal/Thick - made the actual lines of the gun's reticle bolder and thus more apparent) - Reticle opacity (Slider - self-explanatory) - Low Health Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are coloured when James is injured) - Splatter Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are splattered when James is attacked)  INTERACTIONS - Interaction Icon Visibility (Off/Icon/Button Icon - choice of display type for interactable items, display just a dot or the button required to interact) - Interaction Icon Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - displays the previous setting much smaller or larger than default for easy spotting)  GRAPHICS - Colourblind Mode (Normal vision/Deuteranope/Protanope/Tritanope - self-explanatory) - Colourblind Mode Severity (Slider - changes vibrancy of colour-altered effects) - High Contrast Mode (Off/On - makes all scenery monochromatic grey, completely recolouring allies, enemies, environmental interactables, save points, and James himself for visibility. When "on", able to select White/Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Red/Green/Blue for each individual specified model.)  AUDIO  - Night Mode (Off/On - dampens the effect of typical loud sounds like "bang"s)  TEXTS  - Non-Verbal Captions Visibility (Off/On - things like *gate creaks*, and notable ambient sounds captioned) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size Font (Default/Bold/Dyslexic - self-explanatory.) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - self-explanatory) - Subtitle Names (Off/On - tells you who the speaker is in subtitled-text)  Each of these settings are located where you'd expect to find them depending on topic, however there is an additional screen entitled ACCESSIBILITY where it compiles all of these settings into one place for easy-access. It blew my mind that this game had so many options including a dedicated font for dyslexia. I nearly cried. I have OpenDyslexic font installed on my browser so that I can easily digest long strings of information when surfing the web. I never thought I'd actually see it implemented in a video-game.   I purchased the game from an external retailer, but on Steam, this title currently stands at $102.50 AUD. I'm uncertain if that's the same or much lower than what I paid upon release, but I believe it's reasonable for the overall fantastic experience this game provided.

review: A fully fleshed out game (pun intended). It can be hard to justify $70, but this game was truly an extended, immersive experience.   Pros: -The level of detail and the graphics are INSANE. The characters are much more realistic. (when i heard it was "woke" i knew it was gonna be good). From pictures/screenshots it may seem like the characters look odd, but when you're actually in the game & interacting with them: its much more realistic, emotive, detailed, and it all makes sense. It gives "Monster House" for adults vibes. -New endings -New puzzles -It honored not only the original Silent Hill 2 game- but also the original and all of the games by Team Silent. -More immersion into the world -The combat is MUCH smoother -This game fills in a lot of the gaps in the original SH2. You still have to infer things, and its still FILLED with metaphors: but everything is more fully fleshed out. I do think it aligns with what the original idea that Team Silent had, back when they made it. But back in the day: PS2 games were rarely this long. So you had to draw a lot of conclusions yourself, or look up theories. I like that this was a fully-told, hauntingly-beautiful, story. -There is no such thing as "Easy" mode. There is a "Light" mode, which is still extremely challenging & difficult to do. I dont know if this is a pro, or a con, but I know a lot of gamers like to be challenged: so im including it with the pros.  Cons: -There is a bug during the Xray puzzle: where the x-rays that were initially on the wall: disappear when you come back, after collecting the missing x-ray. To fix this: go save your game, reload it, and all of the photos should be there when you load it up again. -Some items just cannot be picked up. This didnt affect gameplay or success though. -Some small visual bugs like guns not physically appearing in hands, but you can still shoot them -The voices were really hard to hear over the sound effects. I wish there was a way to turn that up, without having explosive audio shortly afterwards. -Some of the puzzles, even on light mode: are nearly impossible without a guide. There are just no hints at all for some of the puzzles, and you basically just have to figure it out. So you would be there for many hours. -Silent Hill loves a good prison segment, honey. And of course the prison portion of this game is the most maddening & the worst.

review: Just finished this.   I gotta be honest with you, I think I was expecting more from a name as legendary in the gaming industry as Silent Hill 2.  Before playing, I was excited to finally be able to play Silent Hill 2 after hearing about it for literal decades. Frequently said to be the scariest game ever made, and the story regularly praised to the moon and back.  After playing, I was just kind of relieved that I was just over and done with the game. The game just feels far too bloated for how basic the gameplay is.  While I appreciated a lot of what the game has to offer, I did like the puzzles, the gameplay does feel draining after a while since there is literally only like 4 enemies in the game you'll be fighting against. See one of the basic enemies? Hit it with a pipe and dodge away before it blows up. Puppets? Beat the shit out of them with your pipe. Nurses? Beat the shit out of them with our pipe and occasionally gun them down if you don't feel like dealing with them. Repeat 15+ hours. The solution is every encounter is beating the shit out of everything with your pipe. It doesn't feel like an issue in the first half though, but you'll definitely feel the lack of gameplay variety as the game goes on. I was really feeling it by the time I reached the prison, and that's about 3/5 through the game. On top of that, Silent Hill 2 never really felt scary to me. I can name maybe 3 instances in the entire game where I was a little spooked. Tense and creepy? Yes. Scary? Rarely. Silent Hill 2 is probably a little bit scarier than RE4 Remake, less scary than Dead Space Remake. But that's coming from a major fan of Resident Evil 7, RE8's House Beneviento section, Outlast and Alien Isolation, so of course my expectations were gonna be high when it comes to scare factor.   Don't get me wrong, Silent Hill 2 has a lot of cool moments. The first half is excellent. Extremely dreadful, extremely tense, always masterfully pulling you along and asking yourself what is going to happen next, and how James's story is going to be slowly unravelled. The environments are incredibly detailed, atmosphere is harrowing as hell, the process of figuring out puzzles is really fun, music is haunting (but occasionally cheesy), exploration and level design is fun, boss fights are fun (except maybe the last two boss fights). Unfortunately, most of the game's narrative feels like an illogical carrot on a string. It unravels itself, yes, but it doesn't ever really give you a satisfying climax in the way I was expecting. It just stays in this wierd, vague, mysterious, ambiguous, nightmarish limbo that the rest of the story was submerged in. Always teasing you with something more, and barely delivering, letting the human mind fill the gaps. But I guess that's just the draw for Silent Hill. Everything is illogical. Even the enemy designs are that way. Things in Silent Hill are rarely explained, and when something IS explained, it's generally extremely vague, just enough to give you an idea of what is going on in this twisted and foggy town. Personally, I prefer something a little more blunt, storytelling wise.  I will say that I commend Luke Roberts's voice acting performance. He did a fantastic job. I will also say that Bloober Team has made a pretty good game here, against all odds. Before, Bloober has made incredibly mediocre games, so of course people were expecting this game to be mediocre as well. Bloober proved the doubters wrong. Silent Hill 2 Remake proves that Bloober has the talent to make something genuinely good.  I enjoyed this game, (I LOOOOVED this one section with Angela in particular) I just hope that Bloober continually improves themselves and learns from their experience with this game so we can get something truly incredible from them in the future, I think it'll be a while before that happens though.  8/10

review: I want to start off this review by saying that I have never played the original Silent Hill 2. I don't know if this remake "holds-up" or is as good as the original. With that being said this is one of the greatest horror games ever made, and one of the greatest stories in general. The combat is fun but not too crazy, but at the same time you are kept on your toes. The puzzles are challenging but not too difficult that they become frustrating, and so it is really satisfying to solve them. The graphics are amazing, all the little details around the town, you can tell they really thought this out. The locations are iconic and memorable. The sound design is some of the best I've heard in a video game. Not because it is insanely innovative or anything, but I've never been so afraid in a game solely because of the noises I would hear. There's a part where you're in a dark tunnel and you hear what sounds like giant footsteps clambering towards you. I was in immense panic and kept running out of the tunnel, thinking something was chasing me. But, upon further inspection, it was some kind of creature under the grates on the floor crawling around. All this to say, is that the sound design produced stress, paranoia, and genuine fear into me while playing. The story is really well done. [spoiler] I already had known the big plot twist, but I still was surprised at certain parts and it still is a good game even if you have had it spoiled to you. [/spoiler] Please go into the game as blind as possible. The characters are all interesting as you learn more about them. I will say sometimes the facial animation in cutscenes can feel a little off, but it's not too bad. When you finish the game, you start to see all the symbolism the game uses. (I mean, I didn't understand what the heck was happening), and I highly recommend reading about it online or watching a video about it after playing the game. Silent Hill 2 is one of the best horror games, and video games in general. I wouldn't exactly recommend it at the price it's listed as of writing this review (70$), but if it's on sale definitely grab it. Even if you don't do well with horror games, you should still try it. It doesn't heavily rely on jumpscares, but rather it has building tension and fear through the unknown. Overall an excellent game and well worth your time.

review: This is a survival horror masterpiece, independent of your appreciation of the original. It has the best of everything that survival horror has to offer, and then some.   The combat is mechanically deep enough to incorporate strategy, and there is a fair bit of it. I like the new combat a lot, the enemies are fast and erratic and James is slow and unsteady. Enemies will scatter and hide in the dark, and ambush you with perfect timing. It's more grounded than games like Resident Evil 4 or Dead Space, but still more action heavy than the original silent hill. Despite the frequency of combat, I still found encounters to be tense and mannequins provided relentless jump scares. The bosses were overall great, and a large improvement to the originals as well.  The puzzles and exploration are what separates this from a lot of other modern, OTS camera style horror games. There are a lot of puzzles, and they are elaborate, multi-step processes that carry over into other rooms, that are usually locked by keys or puzzle sequences linked to other rooms. Nearly every section of the game is like a maze, nothing is ever a straight line and you can never tell what's ahead because it's either too dark, or too foggy.   You're constantly feeling lost while being hunted in the dark, scavenging through run down buildings filled with monsters and dark imagery. The sound design brings it all together, with haunting music and sounds that generally make me want to quit the game. Silent Hill's music has the worst vibes, a symphony of sirens, metal banging on metal, strange distortions, all designed to make you feel bad. It's a perfect horror soundtrack.  It's a pretty long game, 16-20 hours for a first run. Every mechanic gets used to its full potential, there is a lot of combat, a lot of puzzles, and a lot of ground to explore. It remains faithful to the original while providing an even more hardcore experience and more challenging level design. Technical issues aside, it's a must play.

review: Wife guy horror game (defo not lots of those around).  In all seriousness, amazing game all around.  Level design: this is where the game shines and brings most of its elements together. If you haven't played a Silent Hill game, think of it like a Resident Evil game (closest comparable example I can think of is RE2R). It's a lot about exploring paths and solving puzzles, all while threading through perilous paths and challenging encounters (all heightened by the spooky aspect of the game). Enemy placements never feel unfair (aside from a few challenging encounters towards the end, but they're meant to be hard), but do require situational awareness. Puzzles (and level progress) is always rewarding (it's never too cut and clear but neither too hard, while still requiring some fair brain power for some).  Story and themes: a refined version of the original (imo), and the original is well remembered for a reason. I can't really go into the story itself, but if you haven't played it, there are 2 questions that you should keep in mind: "What is Silent Hill (and its purpose)?" and "Why are the present people here?". It explores deep themes of psychology, while making good use of presentation through gameplay more so than cinematics (which makes it paying attention all the more rewarding, but it isn't the level of interpretation from Soulsborne games if you're worried). There's also some subtle choices the game never makes you aware of that dictate the end of the game (an important aspect is related to a key game mechanic, but it's up to you to guess), instead of having the obvious "choose your ending" options (although if you really don't want to screw yourself over you can always save at the end of the game, as there will be a "choice" before your final confrontation).  Gameplay: as previously mentioned, puzzles and map exploration are great (which is why I urge to not use guides, even when you struggle). The combat is probably the weak point of the game (although this doesn't mean it's bad). Melee never ever really changes throughout the game (you only need to learn a new enemy's attack pattern every so often), and it will most likely be your main recourse as standard enemies are pretty manageable and saving ammo for tough/boss encounters is vital. Gunplay is serviceable (standard third person shooting). However enemies are pretty fun to fight, and the diversity in how they attack you helps making combat fresh for every encounter (accentuated by the level design). Boss fights are also really great (one of which is probably amongst the best in terms of "what makes a good horror game boss fight?"). While your offensive capabilities are "simple" how they are used for which enemies and which scenarios is what makes combat good.  Art direction: one of the best in horror games. The soundtrack and sound design never misses. The world and levels are scary as they are enthralling. The otherworld (and fogworld) are still one of the most unique horror aesthetics conceived. They manage to perfectly capture the feelings of "you shouldn't be here" and "this place shouldn't exist". The environments are filled with gloominess and hopelessness, with shards of hope.  The horror: excellent. The main emotion felt is "uneasy" with certain high tension scenarios. It never goes for the jumpscares, but rather heavily relies on its suspense and slow built-up for the majority of the game, which makes the tense scenarios even more impactful when they do actually happen. The first quarter of the game is mostly used to introduce its world and workings, while the last quarter is where they bump up the horror aspect.

review: First time playing a game from the series so hopefully this review serves as a barometer of sorts for those looking to break into the series. My experience was on a 4080 Super/13700k PC. As many reviews and news outlets have reported, the game suffers from consistent stuttering and hitching which depending on your sensitivity to that will possibly cause you to refund/uninstall or wait out hoping for Bloober to fix it (they won't and they kinda can't to some degree).   At first, I won't lie, it was really annoying to still deal with traversal stutter despite a shader compilation step and adding some mods that supposedly helped to further improve this via a guide here on Steam. I can't say for certain whether they really helped or not. I did not try playing without the mods to see if there was a change. I also did not play at release so it is hard for me to compare my experience to what apparently was an even worse one at launch. As of this time, there hasn't been a patch to the game in several months and like I mentioned above, Bloober will probably not fix this. To some degree, this is a UE5 issue that would require upgrading the engine version used. Newer versions of the engine have apparently added fixes to stuttering/hitching that we've all come to characterize as a fundamental part of playing a game using UE5. From what i've read/heard, this is not exactly easy nor inexpensive to do and so I doubt they will do so especially when they're already working on the remake for the first SH game. On top of that, they're probably also still doling out support for their newer game Chronos: The New Dawn.   To be very clear, I am not excusing this at all. I found it extremely annoying to have lurches while playing despite traversing areas that should have already had all their assets loaded/streamed in the first time. And that is still not acceptable on the first time as well when the shader compilation step is supposed to take care of that. A lot of the games being released now on UE5 all have these issues no matter if its a PC or console version and hence this is something that will only be fixed in time as devs use newer versions of UE5 that have somewhat tackled these engine-level issues. Is it true that devs also have a responsibility here? Definitely. But these recurring issues with UE5 are a problem with the engine itself more so than with developers using UE5.  Anyways, enough of UE5 stuttering issues. The only other visual oddity to me was the game's sort of mixed bag in terms of its presentation. What I mean here is that the game has a habit of both looking good and oddly bad at the same time. There's lots of aliasing, some environments look muddy and of lower quality than other sections in the game, the water was especially bad looking, etc.. Yet, I persisted.  So why did I persist and why am I ultimately recommending this game? Honestly, its because it does horror and atmosphere well which is what I wanted. There's a sort of surreal and dreamy quality as well as goofiness that often reminds me of Twin Peaks which I am huge fan of. There are twists you don't expect and terribly awful things that happen which depending on how you look at them, either help to villanize or endear characters to you. You feel empathy, pity, disgust, bewildered, etc at the various actions they take and their histories which slowly reveal themselves. The game seriously is a slow burn and this is what I hope you take away from the review the most, that if you continue you will be rewarded. I remember thinking about an hour and half in that I was gonna quit cause of the stuttering and the somewhat obtuse map system. The game is also a lot less hand-holdy than other more modern-horror games like the RE remakes.  The puzzles can be a bit confusing but they're definitely more interesting than those I've experienced. The enemies are grotesque, but they are not so oppressive and terrifying in comparison to the atmosphere, sound design, and the environments (despite their somewhat not visually appealing presentation). This is where the horror genre has to excel for me. The tension should be not facing the monsters, but the environment that has allowed them to exist and flourish in.  Again, the BIG TAKEAWAY here is that if you can get over the game's stuttering/mixed presentation is that the rest of the game really takes you on a journey dealing with themes of abuse, trauma, guilt, not belonging, anger, sadness, etc. The game deals with emotions and events that are deeply human and that paint the road to recovery as one marked with many mistakes, backtracking, and even maybe never actually recovering from the ordeal. I played this consistently once I got over my hump and I think that is solely because I wanted to keep going and experience more of the world and the sheer horror. Do yourself a favor,  play the game.

review: [h1]Silent Hill 2 Review[/h1]  [h2]TL;DR[/h2] This was my (Meta) first entry in the Silent Hills series, and man - what a masterpiece. It's feels like a perfect middle-ground between Resident Evil and Outlast. First playthrough was 15+ hours and it all felt amazing.  [h3]Gameplay[/h3] [list] [*][b]Combat:[/b] You're not a soldier like in RE games, and you're not a journalist like Outlast. You're a normal guy who can lay pipe.  [*][b]Replayability:[/b] Fairly high. Eight endings and NG+  [*][b]Controls:[/b] Slow, but by design. Entering rooms and rounding corners feels terrifying. [/list]  [h3]Story & World[/h3] [list] [*][b]Premise:[/b] James Sunderland arrives in Silent Hill after receiving a letter from his wife (who’s been dead for years). What follows is a descent into guilt, grief, and psychological torment.  [*][b]Characters:[/b] The characters and enemies are so well done. Every scene with Angela felt so powerful.  [*][b]Worldbuilding:[/b] Silent Hill has life(?) but feels so lonely. Atmosphere pulls you in. [/list]  [h3]Progression[/h3] [list] [*][b]100%-able?:[/b] Yes, and seems to be worth it. Each ending gives you another piece of the puzzle.  [*][b]Leveling:[/b] None, you're really just progressing through James' mind.  [*][b]Gear & Tools:[/b] Flashlight, radio, gun, pipe. Every item matters. [/list]  [h3]Presentation[/h3] [list] [*][b]Visuals:[/b] Everything feels so grotesque and unique. I imagine playing the OG was even better.  [*][b]Audio:[/b] Anxiety inducing and amazing.  [*][b]Performance:[/b] Ran fine until one cutscene, and then I dropped frames to 60fps for stream. [/list]  [h3]Bonus Bits[/h3] [list] [*][b]Mods:[/b] Not sure any are out there, or needed.  [*][b]Multiplayer:[/b] None. Silent Hill is a lonely experience.  [*][b]Steam Deck:[/b] I don't believe it's officially supported, and I don't think you'd get the same experience. [/list]

review: Silent Hill 2 - and really the entire franchise - is a unique experience in gaming. When I played the original back in my school years, I felt hopelessness, deep sorrow, and fear. For me, it was the scariest game ever – it didn’t frighten me with jump scares, but with its suffocating atmosphere. Twenty years have passed, and nothing has changed.   The remake crushes you with that same atmosphere from start to finish, carried by the legendary soundtrack of Akira Yamaoka. This is the only game where it feels literally uncomfortable to be there. You want to turn it off, to escape from it - and that is exactly where Bloober succeeded brilliantly.   Yes, there are plenty of excellent survival horrors - Alan Wake 2, Resident Evil 2, 4, 7, 8 - but only in Silent Hill 2 will you feel this. And that’s why the game remains one of a kind.   It’s also unique because of its story - so personal, so intimate for each of its characters: James, Angela, Eddie. If you love narratives rich with psychological depth, this is your game.   And for those who played the original, Bloober prepared surprises: Glimpses of the Past that reference specific moments, scenes, or items from the original game and two completely new endings. Both are worthy of the original, and one of them is so powerful it gives you chills – and you even think, “Yes, this might be the best ending for James.”   An unforgettable game. A unique survival horror. A one-of-a-kind experience that gets under your skin and never lets go.

La primera vez que lo jugué fue en la década de los 2000, cuando todavía no llegaba a los 15 años. No logré pasar ni un tercio porque me daba demasiado miedo, así que terminé abandonándolo.  Hoy, muchos años después, me doy cuenta de algo más fuerte: no solo no lo iba a terminar, sino que tampoco lo iba a entender. Este Silent Hill no se limita a dar miedo con monstruos o escenarios oscuros, sino que toca el verdadero terror: el que genera nuestra propia mente. Habla de traumas, de culpas, de rencores… y nos muestra que la batalla más grande es contra nosotros mismos.  Como decía Carl Jung con el concepto de la sombra, este juego nos enfrenta con esa parte oscura de nuestra psique que escondemos por miedo. En ese sentido, Silent Hill 2 Remake es tan realista como perturbador: no se trata solo de sobrevivir, sino de mirarnos en un espejo incómodo.  Lo recomiendo a quienes estén preparados para algo más que un survival horror. Porque puede ayudarnos a ser más sinceros con nosotros mismos y, en consecuencia, también con los demás.  ⸻  ✅ Puntos positivos: • Una historia profunda y psicológica. • Terror que trasciende lo superficial. • Personajes y atmósfera que dejan huella. • Excelente reinterpretación en el remake.  ❌ Puntos negativos: • No es para cualquiera: puede ser demasiado perturbador. • Jugabilidad que en algunos momentos se siente pesada. • Exige estar en el “estado mental” correcto para apreciarlo.  ⸻  🎯 Conclusión:  Más que un juego de terror, es un viaje a lo más oscuro de la mente humana. Silent Hill 2 Remake no solo asusta: confronta, incomoda y deja pensando. Una experiencia única para quienes se animen a mirarse dentro.  🔸 PUNTUACIÓN FINAL: 9/10 El miedo más real es el que llevamos dentro.  ⸻  📝 REVIEW IN ENGLISH  🔶 The deepest fear doesn’t come from the outside — it comes from within.  ⸻  Let me share a bit of my story with this game. The first time I played it was back in the 2000s, when I was under 15 years old. I couldn’t get past even a third of the game because it scared me so much, so I abandoned it.  Today, looking back as an adult, I realize something bigger: not only was I not going to finish it, I wasn’t even going to understand it. This Silent Hill doesn’t just scare with monsters or dark environments — it dives into the fear created by our own minds. It’s about trauma, guilt, resentment… and it shows us that the greatest battle is against ourselves.  As Carl Jung described with the concept of the shadow, this game confronts us with the darkest part of our psyche that we hide out of fear. In that sense, Silent Hill 2 Remake is as realistic as it is disturbing: it’s not just about surviving, it’s about facing an uncomfortable reflection.  I recommend it to those who are ready for something deeper than a survival horror. It can genuinely help us treat ourselves — and others — more sincerely.  ⸻  ✅ Pros: • Deep, psychological storytelling. • Fear that goes beyond the superficial. • Memorable characters and atmosphere. • Strong reinterpretation in the remake.  ❌ Cons: • Not for everyone: can be too disturbing. • Gameplay can feel heavy at times. • Requires the right mental state to fully appreciate.  ⸻  🎯 Conclusion:  More than a horror game, it’s a journey into the darkest corners of the human mind. Silent Hill 2 Remake doesn’t just scare — it confronts, unsettles, and lingers. A unique experience for those brave enough to look within.  🔸 FINAL SCORE: 9/10 The scariest fear is the one we carry inside.

review: Silent hill de modo geral, é uma franquia que conheço e gosto desde a minha infância, sendo para mim a melhor franquia de games, e o 2 foi minha porta de entrada para a franquia, sendo para mim um dos melhores games que já tive o prazer de zerar. Minha primeira oportunidade de zerar foi em 2017, a franquia já estava "morta", mas mesmo assim foi uma das minhas maiores obeseçoes, jogar todos os games, ler tudo que é possível do game, e considero uma franquia que nunca vai ser batida por qualquer outra.  Questão de personagens e sua caracterizações, a Ângela foi a melhor no game original já era no remake mais ainda, Maria não tenho muito oque comentar sobre ela, Laura melhorou, Eddie no começo não gostei muito dele, gostava do personagem no original e achava ele de certo modo patético, mas entendia o motivo aqui a princípio era apenas patético, mas chegando na prisão mudei completamente minha opinião, James gostei muito, ele continua caladão como ele deve ser e era no original, mas aqui sinto ele mais humano e melhor, e por fim, Mary, mas Mary e a Mary não tem como não gostar dela.  Questão do combate gostei em partes a Mannequim é realmente oque ela representa não tem como rejeitar a realidade é um bicho insuportável, Nurse eu gostei do moveset dela, Pyramid Head ele é ele foda demais, Abstract Daddy apenas nojento e repugnante, Flesh Lips questão de modelo e significado esse é um dos melhores, Mandarins chato para um krl, Mary Boss bos bom e com muito significado para a trama.   Trilha sonora espetacular como a de todos silent hill, nada a reclamar, o thema da Laura não tem igual, lindo.  E por fim, foi um jogasso, confesso que algumas me deixaram meio pá por questão de algumas mudanças, mas nada dms, 100/100, mas o original continua sendo bem superior em tudo, confesso que possa ser um certo saudosismo da minha parte, mas é um bom game.  Único paia que peguei que para mim é um dos piores finais, vsfd.  "In my restless dreams, I see that town.  Silent Hill.  You promised me you'd take me there again someday. But you never did.  Well, I'm alone there now... In our 'special place'... Waiting for you...  Waiting for you to come to see me.  But you never do.  And so I wait, wrapped in my cocoon of pain and loneliness.  I know I've done a terrible thing to you. Something you'll never forgive me for.  I wish I could change that, but I can't.  I feel so pathetic and ugly laying here, waiting for you...  Every day I stare up at the cracks in the ceiling and all I can think about is how unfair it all is...  The doctor came today. He told me I could go home for a short stay.  It’s not that I'm getting better. It’s just that this may be my last chance...  I think you know what I mean...  Even so, I'm glad to be coming home. I've missed you terribly.  But I'm afraid, James. I'm afraid you don't really want me to come home.  Whenever you come see me, I can tell how hard it is on you...  I don't know if you hate me or pity me... Or maybe I just disgust you...  I'm sorry about that.  When I first learned that I was going to die, I just didn't want to accept it.  I was so angry all the time and I struck out at everyone I loved most. Especially you, James.  That's why I understand if you do hate me.  But I want you to know this, James.  I'll always love you.  Even though our life together had to end like this, I still wouldn't trade it for the world. We had some wonderful years together.  Well, this letter has gone on too long, so I'll say goodbye.  I told the nurse to give this to you after I'm gone.  That means that as you read this, I'm already dead.  I can't tell you to remember me, but I can't bear for you to forget me.  These last few years since I became ill...
